response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps cumulative exposure only through the product q*D*tau with a single constant infectivity gain beta_inf, giving a pure exponential dose-time relation p_inf = 1 - exp(-beta_inf*q*D*tau).
response_change.child_relation: Replace the assumption of constant per-unit infectivity with a dose-dependent effective infectivity so the hazard rises sublinearly at higher D, while remaining increasing in q, D, and tau.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed q, equal increases in duration produce nearly proportional risk changes at low D but smaller incremental risk gains at high D than the parent predicts; equivalently, the p_inf-versus-D curve bends more strongly downward before final probability saturation.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when D spans a range from dilute to sufficiently high standardized infectious-unit levels that within-dose heterogeneity or aggregation reduces marginal infectivity per additional unit, with environmental conditions fixed and q, tau varied within ranges that keep p_inf away from complete saturation for at least part of the data.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the mechanism appears as weaker-than-parent dose escalation at higher D even after fitting beta_inf; in holdout, the same curvature difference extends to longer tau or larger q where the parent's single gain overpredicts risk at high D while matching low-D behavior.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of negligible dose-dependent infectivity modulation, the effective infectivity becomes constant and the parent law p_inf = 1 - exp(-beta_inf*q*D*tau) is recovered.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every additional infectious unit is equally potent regardless of dose level, so only total cumulative exposure matters and the dose-response shape is fixed by one gain parameter.
plan.baseline_assumption: All infectious units have the same average ability to initiate infection.
plan.scientific_mechanism: At higher inhaled dose levels, infectious units can be partially redundant because of clumping, overlap in target-site access, or heterogeneous viability within the inhaled inoculum, causing diminishing marginal infectivity per added unit.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's constant-per-unit infectivity assumption rather than add a wholly new process. The parent response is a one-parameter exponential in the single coordinate q*D*tau, so at fixed q it predicts the same curvature pattern in D for all tau after rescaling by beta_inf. Under fixed environmental conditions, vary D across low to moderately high levels and compare short versus long tau. The child mechanism predicts that higher D becomes less efficient per unit than lower D, so risk still increases monotonically with D and tau but with stronger concavity in D than the parent. This changes the scored mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary quantity. A single refitted parent beta_inf cannot match both the low-D slope and the reduced high-D marginal increase across those conditions, because its only shape control is the final exponential saturation in p_inf, not pre-saturation dose-dependent weakening of infectivity. The contrast is scientifically admissible when the standardized dose range is broad enough for redundancy/clumping effects to matter but not so extreme that all observations are already near p_inf≈1, where the distinction becomes hard to see.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when exposure duration spans from short to long enough that within-episode attenuation can accumulate, while D is in a nonzero admissible range and environmental conditions remain fixed; strongest when tau covers at least order-unity variation relative to the attenuation timescale.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as weaker-than-linear growth of infection pressure with tau at fixed D and q; in holdout, the same attenuation extends to longer tau or higher qD combinations, yielding stronger long-duration flattening without changing the short-duration limit.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the within-episode attenuation strength tends to zero, so effective infectivity remains constant over the exposure and cumulative pressure again scales linearly with tau.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes infection-initiation efficiency is constant throughout the exposure episode, so every additional hour contributes the same expected hazard at fixed D and q after only dose-crowding is accounted for.
plan.baseline_assumption: Host susceptibility remains fixed during an exposure episode and all infectious units have the same average ability to initiate infection over the full duration.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Within a single episode, the earliest inhaled pathogens may preferentially exploit the most accessible target sites, or rapid local protective responses may reduce later marginal establishment probability, causing time-dependent attenuation of effective infectivity.
plan.rationale: Vary tau while holding environmental conditions fixed and comparing curves across fixed D and q. The parent predicts one shared linear-in-tau infection pressure before the outer saturation, so after refitting beta_inf and alpha_clump it still cannot create a systematic extra flattening that appears only at longer tau while preserving the same short-tau slope structure across conditions. A child with within-episode attenuation changes the scored mapping itself: p_inf versus tau bends downward more strongly at long durations, especially when baseline infection pressure beta_inf*q*D/(1+alpha_clump*D) is appreciable. This is scientifically admissible for single exposure episodes long enough for target-site depletion or rapid local defenses to matter, but the effect may be weak for very short episodes, very low D, or very low q, where the parent remains a good approximation.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when exposure durations include a short-episode regime comparable to the pathogen establishment timescale, while D and q are held fixed and environmental conditions remain fixed; negligible in long episodes where the lag is small relative to tau.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, variation across short versus moderate tau at the same D can show reduced initial slope; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to dose-dependent interplay because lag-induced early suppression and existing late-time attenuation jointly reshape the tau response.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing establishment lag timescale relative to all sampled tau, or when analysis is restricted to episodes much longer than that lag.
plan.promotion_reason: A finite onset lag cannot be activated from only D, tau, q and the existing fixed parameters without introducing a separate timescale; the parent already uses all current symbols for dose crowding and within-episode attenuation, so an independently sampled episode-condition or pathogen-property lag input is needed to distinguish short episodes from long ones beyond simple refitting.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes infectious units begin contributing to infection initiation immediately upon inhalation, with no explicit within-episode establishment delay.
plan.baseline_assumption: All infectious units have the same average ability to initiate infection, effectively with instantaneous onset of infectivity once inhaled during the episode.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite transit/attachment/penetration time before inhaled pathogens can start productive establishment, creating an early-time lag within the exposure episode before the existing attenuation-limited accumulation dominates.
plan.rationale: Vary tau while holding D, q, and environment fixed. In the parent, p_inf rises immediately with nonzero initial slope at tau near 0 because every moment of exposure contributes instantly, only tempered by attenuation. A realistic refinement is a finite within-episode establishment lag: newly inhaled pathogens may require transport through mucus or attachment before they can initiate infection. Then the child has a flatter short-tau response and delayed curvature, while remaining nondecreasing and bounded by 1. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because the scored p_inf versus tau relation differs directly. The contrast is scientifically admissible for short exposure episodes comparable to the lag timescale; for much longer episodes, the effect fades and the parent is approximately recovered. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both an explicit early-time suppression and the same longer-tau behavior across these conditions, because changing beta_inf, gamma_att, or delta_dose_att rescales or retunes one-phase accumulation but does not create a separate onset timescale distinct from later attenuation.

diagnostic_groups.name: att_load
diagnostic_groups.role: Within-episode attenuation burden; identifies regimes where altered establishment timing remains observable before late-time attenuation dominates.

contract.activation_condition: Most visible when tau is of order tau_est (x_lag around 0.3 to a few) and att_load is not already very large, so the episode samples the onset regime rather than only the long-time attenuated regime.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as systematic deviation from a single universal onset-lag shape across short and intermediate tau. In holdout, the same distributed-delay effect extends to broader tau/tau_est ranges while preserving the same long-duration parent-like behavior.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the distributed-delay shape back to the single-timescale limit so effective establishment approaches the original 1 - exp(-tau/tau_est) factor.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Heterogeneity in airway deposition depth, mucus transport, attachment, and penetration creates a distribution of establishment delays across inhaled infectious units within an episode.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the establishment kernel itself, introducing a different saturating onset law in tau/tau_est rather than merely rescaling infection pressure.
contract.assumption_before: Finite transit/attachment/penetration delay is represented by one common exponential establishment-lag factor with a single characteristic time tau_est.
contract.assumption_after: Establishment delays are broadly distributed, so cumulative effective establishment during the episode follows a saturating delay-response rather than one single-phase exponential turn-on.
contract.parent_reduction: The child is intended as a broader-delay continuation of the same mechanism; the parent is recovered conceptually by narrowing the delay distribution back toward the original single-phase establishment law.
contract.observable_signature: Holding D, q, and environmental conditions fixed while varying tau, the parent gives one shared onset-lag shape through 1 - exp(-tau/tau_est), whereas the child gives a different saturating onset kernel ((tau/tau_est)/(1 + tau/tau_est)). The scored mapping p_inf(tau) therefore shows changed short-to-intermediate curvature when tau is comparable to tau_est, especially before attenuation load becomes dominant.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally match both the earliest suppression and the broader intermediate turn-on across these conditions because the parent has only one characteristic lag-shape family, controlled by tau_est as a location/scale parameter. Refitting beta_inf, tau_est, or attenuation parameters rescales or shifts the onset but does not create the altered curvature of the establishment kernel itself.
